coverage: Round-2 finder on the Martin MEASUREMENT angle, continuing a predecessor cut off at 18 sources / 49 claims. NAMED ROSTER: Spathis (fetched by the predecessor; adverb scarcity and dropped -ly counted separately in its claims) - FETCHED; Ben Blatt, Nabokov's Favorite Word Is Mauve, 'Use Sparingly' - FETCHED snippet-only via Google Books SearchWithinVolume2 (volume 0AhHDgAAQBAJ, recovered through books?vid=ISBN9781501105388 after the Books API hit its daily quota): Blatt's corpus does include eight Martin novels and Martin is among his fifty example authors, but a full-text search returns his name on no page of the Use Sparingly chapter, so the adverb chapter appears not to print a Martin figure; David J. Peterson, The Art of Language Invention (2015) - FETCHED in full (archive.org OCR text) and it answers the angle's question directly: fifty-six Dothraki words and names in the first three books, twenty-four of them proper names, and six High Valyrian words; dothraki.com - FETCHED by the predecessor; WordsRated chapter-length figures - the roster URL wordsrated.com/a-song-of-ice-and-fire-statistics/ is a 404 (NOT FOUND); the live page game-of-thrones-stats was read by the predecessor and carries only per-book chapter totals, so chapter-length was covered instead from the A Song of Ice and Fire Wiki's chapter-by-chapter table. BLOCKED: the Ukrainian archaism study (apiph.eenu.edu.ua, host unreachable); prosecraft.io itself (site dead, only its A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms page is in the Wayback Machine); iceandfire.fandom.com and wordsrated.com live (Cloudflare/WAF, both recovered through Wayback raw captures). EXPANSION, 11 new substantive sources: bibliography/lateral routes gave the archived prosecraft book page, the Shaxpir methodology post, the AutoCrit measurement of A Game of Thrones, TeachingBooks and LightSail text-complexity records, the Books & Boots affix and compound essay, the ASOIAF Wiki chapter table, a reader's chapter-length count on asoiaf.westeros.org, and - the find of the round - a GitHub scrape of the whole prosecraft library (22,449 books) that carries figures for nine Martin titles including Fire and Blood, letting the maester-chronicle register be compared numerically with the novels. OpenAlex, Crossref-shaped and Semantic-Scholar-shaped searches for Martin stylometry returned nothing new beyond what the predecessor already had; two consecutive lateral searches surfaced nothing new, so discovery stopped. Combined state: 34 sources read, 109 claims.
